issues.issue: D ~ N(0,1) is one reading of 'random Gaussian', but it is 112x off the scale the method's own constraint asks for, and that mismatch changes checkpoint selection for the gauss arm only. As written, both the Q2 contrast (gauss vs zero) and the Q3 TFPS arm depend on this audit-chosen scale through a side channel that has nothing to do with routing, and the only protection (pure-val-MSE re-selection) is non-gating.
issues.evidence: Derived from code. (a) layers/Constraint.py: loss_d1 = 1e-3*||diag(D^T D) - I||_F targets unit-norm columns; loss_d2 = 1e-3*||offblock(D^T D)||_F. For a 112x112 D ~ N(0,1): diag(D^T D) ~ 112, so loss_d1 ~ 1e-3*sqrt(112)*111 ~ 1.18; off-block entries have variance 112 over 9408 entries, so loss_d2 ~ 1e-3*sqrt(9408*112) ~ 1.03. Two EDESC instances with alpha=gama=1 add ~4.4 to the training loss and to the validation loss (exp/exp_main.py:130, :257-262), about 10x the forecast MSE (~0.4). For D=0 the same terms are 2*1e-3*sqrt(112) ~ 0.021 and constant; for D ~ N(0, 1/112) they are ~0.02. (b) EarlyStopping (utils/tools.py:40-63) saves on any decrease of that sum. Under N(0,1) the constraint term falls every epoch while Adam shrinks D (roughly lr per entry per step; my estimate at H=192 is ~0.1 per epoch at first, decaying with the type3 0.9^epoch schedule), which is larger than epoch-to-epoch changes in val MSE for many epochs. So tfps_gauss is likely to save late checkpoints chosen by the constraint term, while tfps_zero selects on val MSE plus a constant. (c) At H=192 (lr 5e-4, type3) Adam can move an entry of D by at most about 5e-4 * 65 steps * ~13 effective epochs ~ 0.4 in total, against an init sd of 1: D stays close to its random draw and cannot reach the constrained set. At sd 1/sqrt(112) ~ 0.094 it can. (d) Cluster.py:68: eta*d = 140 is added to ||z D_i||^2. With N(0,1), ||z D_i||^2 ~ ||z||^2 * chi2_28 (mean 28||z||^2), which swamps 140 for any ||z||^2 above ~5, so s varies across experts by roughly +-27% of 1/4. With unit-norm columns ||z D_i||^2 ~ 0.25||z||^2, so 140 dominates unless ||z||^2 is in the hundreds, and s is almost uniform. So N(0,1) is the scale under which the affinity has the most say in routing (in the paper's favour for Q2) and also the scale that distorts the loss and checkpoint selection (against it for Q2 and Q3). (e) layers/InitializeD.py, the initialiser the repo ships and never calls, returns orthonormal columns (left singular vectors), i.e. the unit-norm scale, not sd 1. An author's advocate would say sd 1 is a strawman on (a), (c) and (e); the audit can answer that sd 1 is the literal default and helps routing on (d). Neither side can be settled from the text.
issues.fix: Do not let one scale carry the verdicts. For Q3 compute the label against each TFPS arm (gauss sd 1, gauss unit, zero); a negative label (VANISHES / REVERSED / SHRINKS) stands only if every TFPS arm gets a label at least that negative, otherwise report 'Q3 DEPENDS ON D INIT' with the per-arm table. issues.issue: The routing qualifier and the noise-off arm are close to decided by the code, and neither tests the paper's mechanism. They are fair as descriptions of the released router, but the labels can be read as 'pattern routing does not work'.
issues.evidence: Derived. s is row-normalised (Cluster.py:69), so every s_i is in [0,1] and the row sums to 1; the router adds randn*softplus(s) (SparseMoE.py:59), whose sd is at least softplus(0) = 0.69 and is 0.83 at s = 0.25. Whatever D is, the noise is several times the spread of s, so A will sit near 1/n = 0.25 and the 0.30 threshold will very likely fire. Even a one-hot s would give A well below 1 (my rough estimate is around 0.5). For arm 3: experts were trained under near-random assignment and top-1 gate weight is exactly 1, so the experts are close to interchangeable and switching the noise off at eval only should change little. Training with noise off is the arm that would test affinity routing, and it is not in the design (owner decision 2 specifies eval only).
issues.fix: Keep both, but (1) state in section 7 that the qualifier is expected from the code and give the ceiling: A for a one-hot s under this router, computed once in step (c) by simulation of the router alone, plus the mean per-row max-min of s for each arm, so A is read against what is attainable; (2) reword the qualifier to 'ROUTER NOISE EXCEEDS AFFINITY SPREAD (A = …, ceiling = …)'; (3) add to section 9: 'whether training with noise-free affinity routing improves accuracy is not tested; NOISE-OFF labels concern evaluation of a model trained with the released noisy router'.

issues.issue: How D is drawn is ambiguous and may either make the two D matrices identical or break the pairing between arms.
issues.evidence: PREREG section 5 arm 1: 'drawn from torch's global RNG right after torch.manual_seed(seed) inside EDESC construction (both instances)'. If manual_seed(seed) is called inside each EDESC.__init__, the time and frequency D (both 112x112) are the same matrix, and the global stream is reset mid-construction, so layers built after each EDESC (SparseMoE experts, heads; PatchTST_MoE_backbone_cluster_time.py:47-65) repeat or shift their draws. If it is not re-seeded, the gauss arm consumes 2*12544 extra draws, so for a given seed every later weight differs from the zero arm and the gauss-zero contrast includes an unrelated re-draw of the experts and heads.

Then gauss and zero share every other initial weight for a given seed; self-test that all non-D parameters are bitwise equal across the two arms at step 0. Report the paired difference across seeds next to the Welch CI (Welch stays the gating rule unless the statistics lens prefers paired).

issues.issue: The N(0,1) scale for D_gauss goes against what the repo shows about the intended scale, and it changes what the released training and selection loop does. That can work against TFPS in Q3.
issues.evidence: Repo evidence on scale: (1) Cluster.py is the EDESC module almost line for line: the 'Subspace bases proxy' comment, the commented-out EDESC line `self.D = Parameter(torch.Tensor(n_z, n_clusters))` at :27, the commented-out AE reconstruction, and 'Eq 9/12/13/15/16' comments. That module never initialises D because its pipeline overwrote it with Initialization_D. (2) InitializeD.py:50-55 sets D from SVD left singular vectors, so columns are orthonormal and entries are about 1/sqrt(n*d) = 0.094. (3) D_constraint1 (Constraint.py:170-173) pulls diag(D^T D) to 1, i.e. unit column norm. None of this states a mean or std, but all three point to unit-norm columns, not N(0,1), whose column norms are about sqrt(112) = 10.6. This lens measured numerically (random z ~ N(0,1), n=4, d=28, no training): under N(0,1), D_constraint1 + D_constraint2 = 1.16 + 0.99 = 2.15 per EDESC, so about 4.3 across the two instances. Forecast MSE is about 0.45. Under N(0,1/112) the same terms are 0.0014 + 0.009. The early-stopping criterion is MSE + alpha*aux + gama*aux (exp_main.py:130,262), so under N(0,1) about 90% of the selection signal at the start is the constraint term. At H=192 (lr 5e-4, type3 decay, about 65 steps per epoch), the total Adam movement per entry is at most about 65*5e-4*13 = 0.42. D therefore cannot shrink to unit columns, and the aux term probably dominates val loss for the whole run. Trade-off: at N(0,1/112), s is nearly uniform (mean row range 0.023; noisy-top1 vs argmax agreement 0.26 against chance 0.25). At N(0,1) the range is 0.13 and agreement 0.29. Each scale handicaps a different part of the method.
issues.fix: Prefer this: pre-register both scales as TFPS arms, N(0,1) and N(0,1/(n*d)) (the EDESC/constraint-consistent scale). Fix the primary now; this lens recommends N(0,1/(n*d)) for Q3, because it does not inflate the released selection loss. A Q2 'INIT MATTERS/EQUIVALENT' label or a Q3 'TFPS loses' label may be stated without a scale qualifier only if it holds under both scales. Cost: about +5-10 CPU-h. Minimum if budget forbids: keep N(0,1), suffix every Q2/Q3 label with 'D ~ N(0,1)', promote the pure-val-MSE checkpoint to a co-reported Q3 table (still non-gating), and log the aux share of val loss at the selected epoch. Remove the claim that N(0,1) 'most literally' reads the paper, or support it from the PDF.

lenses.summary: No verdict family is settled by how the arms are built. tfps_gauss routing does differ from tfps_zero, but only slightly: at init s under D~N(0,1) is close to uniform (mean row max 0.31, mean range 0.11), and noisy top-1 agrees with argmax s on A=0.283 of rows against 0.25 chance. A is capped at about 0.61 even for a one-hot s, so the A<0.30 qualifier can come out either way. The Q2 premise check can be met: measured s range is exactly 0, and the D=0 constraint gradient is finite and exactly 0. The Q3 rules are exhaustive. However, the power text gets the reachability conditions wrong (SHRINKS needs half-width < m_H/2), and the extension trigger inherits that error. A new major confound is that the gauss arm's early-stopping loss is about 90% D-constraint penalty.

issues.issue: Q2 is confounded by checkpoint selection. The early-stopping val loss is MSE + alpha*KL/constraint terms (exp_main.py:130, :257-262). With D~N(0,1) the two D constraints add about 2.23 per EDESC instance, 4.47 for both, which is about 10x the MSE (~0.4-0.5). This penalty depends only on D and falls steadily as Adam shrinks D. With D=0 the aux term is a constant 0.0106 per instance (KL=0, d1=1e-3*sqrt(112), d2=0). So tfps_zero early-stops on val MSE, while tfps_gauss early-stops mostly on how fast D decays. At H=192 (lr 5e-4, ~65 steps/epoch, type3 decay 0.9/epoch from epoch 3), the total Adam travel per D entry over 100 epochs is at most about 5e-4*65*13 = 0.42. That is far from the orthonormal target (entries ~0.09), so the constraint keeps falling for most of the run, and the selected gauss checkpoint is likely late and possibly overfit. Any Q2 Delta (INIT MATTERS or INIT REVERSED) may therefore come from the selection rule rather than from affinity routing. This makes no outcome foregone, but it makes the Q2 labels easy to misread.
issues.evidence: layers/Constraint.py:16-17,38-39 (1e-3*Frobenius norms); measured D_constraint1(N(0,1) 112x112)=1.196, D_constraint2=1.038; N(0,1/112): 0.0014, 0.0092. layers/Cluster.py:86 total = beta*KL + d1 + d2. utils/tools.py:18-19 type3. exp/exp_main.py:55 Adam, no weight decay.
issues.fix: Score Q2 on pure-val-MSE checkpoint selection for both arms. The prereg already saves that checkpoint for the sensitivity analysis, so promote it to co-primary for Q2: a Q2 label holds only if both selections give it, otherwise add a 'SELECTION-DEPENDENT' suffix. Also log, per run, the best epoch and the aux-loss share of the val loss at that epoch. In §5, state that the N(0,1) scale choice sets the aux loss to about 10x the MSE (vs about 0.02x under N(0,1/(n*d))).

issues.issue: The reachability text in §7 is wrong for Q3. SHRINKS needs L_B>0 and U_B<m_H at once, so the CI width must be < m_H, i.e. half-width < m_H/2 (sigma < ~0.0047 at H=192, < ~0.0030 at H=336 under the prereg's own 1.18*sigma). It is not half-width < m_H. SURVIVES has no width condition (it only needs mean d_B > hw). Welch df at n=5 with unequal seed sd (DLinear is close to deterministic, TFPS has eval noise) falls toward 4, so t_0.95 is about 2.13, not 1.86. Because the variance-triggered extension is judged on 'half-width exceeds m_H', it will not fire in exactly the case where SHRINKS is unreachable but VANISHES/SURVIVES are reachable. That biases the outcome away from SHRINKS. The rules can still all be reached, so this is not foregone.
issues.evidence: PREREG §7 power paragraph and the Q3 rules 2-4. Arithmetic: SHRINKS requires d-hw>0 and d+hw<m, so 2hw<m.
issues.fix: Restate each label's reachability condition: SURVIVES none; REVERSED none; VANISHES and INIT EQUIVALENT hw<m_H; SHRINKS hw<m_H/2. Use Welch-Satterthwaite df with the observed sds. Define the extension trigger as 'hw >= m_H/2 for any Q3 baseline comparison, or hw >= m_H for Q2', still judged on width only. Pre-state plausible sigmas: PatchTST ~0.002-0.005, DLinear ~0.0005-0.002, TFPS unknown and possibly larger at lr 5e-3 with eval noise. On those, SHRINKS at H=336 is likely unreachable even at n=10; say so.

issues.issue: Q2 premise and arm-4 numbers for tfps_zero are fixed by construction, and the prereg should say so. With D=0, s is exactly 1/n, so argmax s = index 0 on every row (torch tie-breaking). arm-4 A for tfps_zero is then P(noisy top-1 == expert 0) = 0.25 and H_r = ln 4 ≈ 1.386, apart from sampling error. These values are a calibration reference, not a measurement. (A noise-off arm under D=0 would send every row to expert 0; it is correctly not in the design.)
issues.evidence: Measured on test windows, D=0, released config H=192: s range 0.0 (max = min = 0.25), argmax usage [1,0,0,0], A_time=0.251, A_freq=0.249, H_r=1.386. Constraint grad at D=0: finite, max|grad| = 0.0 (torch 2.4.1), so the premise check is satisfiable.
issues.fix: State that A(tfps_zero) ≈ 0.25 and H_r ≈ ln 4 are expected by construction. Report them as a sanity check (flag if A is outside 0.25 ± 0.02), not as evidence.

issues.issue: The A qualifier threshold (0.30) sits right next to the measured init value (0.283), and the scale of A is not stated. The ceiling of A at n=4 is about 0.61 even for a near-one-hot s (smax 0.97), because the winner's noise sd is softplus(s) ≈ 1.29. Readers will take 'A=0.35' to mean weak routing when it may be about 1/3 of the achievable range.
issues.evidence: Synthetic, 20k rows, 4 experts: smax 0.25→A 0.253; 0.40→0.335; 0.60→0.442; 0.80→0.541; 0.97→0.606. Released model at init with D~N(0,1): A_time 0.283, A_freq 0.284.
issues.fix: Report alongside A the mean row max and range of s, and A_max(s) computed from the observed s with a one-hot reference (or an affinity-to-routing normalisation: (A-0.25)/(A_onehot-0.25)). Keep 0.30 as the pre-registered cut but mention the ceiling.

issues.issue: Small error in a code-line citation. In the time backbone, the permute after the un-permuted cluster reshape is at line 81 (reshape :82, MoE :83, permute back :85), not ':83-87'. The frequency file's ':79 vs :83-87' is correct.
issues.evidence: layers/PatchTST_MoE_backbone_cluster_time.py:77,81-85; layers/PatchTST_MoE_backbone_cluster_frequency.py:79,83-87.
issues.fix: Cite :77 vs :81-85 for the time file.

verified_code_claims: Cluster.py:61-69 affinity formula with eta*d, row-normalised: confirmed (d=28, eta*d=140)
SparseMoE.py:57-66 noisy_logits = s + randn*softplus(s), top-k, no self.training guard: confirmed; with top_k=1 softmax over a single finite logit gives weight exactly 1 (SparseMoE.py:64-65, 103-105)
D=0 fixed point: constraint gradients finite and exactly 0 at D=0 (measured); KL gradient through ||zD_i||^2 is 0 at D=0; Adam with zero grad leaves D unchanged; exp_main.py:55 has no weight decay
exp_main.py:130 val loss = MSE + alpha*cluster_time + gama*cluster_freq: confirmed; :69-71 refined target from detached s
exp_main.py:24 imports Initialization_D: confirmed; :361-365 np.array stacks: confirmed
data_factory.py:17-20 test drop_last True: confirmed; run_longExp.py:84 eta 5, :94 patience 20, :98 lradj type3, :134 setting string: confirmed
etth1.sh:77-89 H=192 lr 5e-4, 4/4 experts, top-1/top-1: confirmed

measurements.setup: released Model (models/PatchTST_MoE_cluster.py) with the H=192 config (d_model 16, e_layers 3, n_heads 4, d_ff 128, 4/4 experts, top-1, eta 5, enc_in 7), torch.manual_seed(2021), eval mode, forward only on the first 4 ETTh1 test batches (12288 cluster rows per router; patch_num_out=24). No training. A is averaged over 20 noise draws.
measurements.gauss_scale_sweep_sd_3_10_30: s range 0.131-0.136, A 0.287-0.289 for both routers. Scaling D does not sharpen s: once ||zD_i||^2 >> eta*d, s_i is proportional to ||zD_i||^2, which is a ratio of chi-square-like terms (28 dof) across random subspaces.

answers.a_routing_gauss_vs_zero: Routing differs, but only a little. Under N(0,1), s is near-uniform, not near-one-hot (row max ~0.31). Noisy top-1 follows argmax s on 28.3% of rows against 25% chance, and expert usage entropy is the same as uniform. At init, gauss routing is close to random, but not exactly random by construction. Training can sharpen s through the KL target, so post-training A is open (range 0.25 to ~0.61).
answers.b_Q2_premise: Satisfiable. Measured max-min of s = 0 exactly, and D stays at 0 (zero gradient).
answers.c_Q3_rules: Exhaustive (rule 5 catches the rest), and each rule is reachable in principle at n=5. SHRINKS needs hw < m_H/2, which is likely unreachable at H=336 for plausible TFPS seed sd, and the extension trigger as written does not cover this case.

verified_clean: Scaler fit on train rows only (data_loader.py:60-62, byte-identical in both repos, sha 1d49e220); RevIN is per-window (instance) normalisation, no cross-split statistics.
Early stopping and the type3 lr schedule read only the val loss: tfps exp_main.py:257,262,267-268; official exp_main.py:199,204,210. test_loss (tfps :258, official :200) is only printed.

Per-epoch test pass cannot change weights or BN: it runs inside vali() under model.eval() + torch.no_grad() (tfps :75-76,134; official :56-57,97); BatchNorm1d in the encoder (backbone_cluster_time.py:262,275) only updates running stats in train mode; total_loss/D_constraint (Cluster.py:72-88, Constraint.py) are pure functions; no buffers or counters are written in forward (SparseMoE.py, Cluster.py:54-70).

Per-epoch test pass does consume global RNG (TFPS router randn_like at eval, SparseMoE.py:59; one base-seed draw per DataLoader iterator in both repos), but the amount consumed depends only on tensor shapes/batch count, never on test values, so it shifts the training RNG stream without carrying test information. PREREG's 'affects nothing but logs and RNG' is correct.

No cross-window mixing in TFPS: the un-permuted reshape (backbone_cluster_time.py:76) keeps rows b*P..(b+1)*P-1 inside sample b, so per-window predictions do not depend on batch composition except through router-noise draws; deriving both scores from one eval pass is therefore valid.

type3 schedule identical in both repos (utils/tools.py:18-19, sha 80c2f839 both). Both repos construct OneCycleLR (tfps exp_main.py:160-164; official :120-124) which sets lr to max_lr/25 at construction (checked: torch 2.4.1, lr=5e-3 -> 2.0e-4) and is never stepped under type3, so epoch 1 trains at lr/25, epochs 2-3 at lr, epoch k>=3 at lr*0.9^(k-3). Symmetric across arms.
Arm 3 (noise-off) reuses the arm-1 checkpoint selected on val only; no test-based choice enters; paired comparison is legitimate.
Val loader shuffle+drop_last (data_factory.py:28-30) identical for all arms; test loader shuffle False, drop_last True (:17-20).

issues.issue: Selection criterion differs systematically between the two Q2 arms (and vs baselines) because of magnitude, not just form. TFPS val loss = MSE + alpha*aux_time + gama*aux_freq (exp_main.py:130). Under D ~ N(0,1) (112x112, d=28) the constraint terms alone are ~1.20 (D_constraint1) + ~1.04 (D_constraint2) per EDESC instance, ~4.5 total for both instances, vs val MSE ~0.45; under D = 0 the aux is the constant 0.0106 per instance (KL = 0, constraint2 = 0). So arm 1 early-stops on a quantity dominated by D's progress towards orthonormality, arm 2 effectively on MSE, baselines on MSE (official exp_main.py:93). With delta=0 (tools.py:41,55) any tiny monotone aux decrease resets patience, so arm 1 may run far more epochs than arm 2 (an epoch-budget asymmetry inside Q2) and its checkpoint may not be its best-forecast epoch.
issues.evidence: tfps exp/exp_main.py:116-121,130,262; layers/Constraint.py:14-17,30-39; layers/Cluster.py:68-69; utils/tools.py:50-63; numeric check of the constraint terms at N(0,1) init (torch 2.4.1, seed 0): 1.196, 1.038; at D=0: 0.0106.
issues.fix: Keep released selection as primary, but (a) log per epoch the val MSE and each aux component separately and epochs-to-stop per run; report mean epochs-to-stop per arm; (b) pre-register that the pure-val-MSE re-selection is applied to every TFPS arm and the Q2/Q3 tables are recomputed on it, and if any label differs from the primary label attach the suffix 'SELECTION-SENSITIVE (pure-val-MSE label: ...)'. State in §2 that the D_gauss scale choice directly sets how much of the stopping criterion is aux (N(0,1/(n·d)) would make aux ~0 at init).

issues.issue: The pure-val-MSE sensitivity hook is placed on Exp_Main.vali, which the training loop calls for BOTH val and test every epoch (exp_main.py:257-258). A hook that does not distinguish the two calls would select the sensitivity checkpoint on test MSE (direct test selection), or alternate between them.
issues.evidence: tfps exp/exp_main.py:73,257,258 (same function, different loaders).
issues.fix: Hook must key on the loader object identity (vali_loader created at :139) or wrap only the first vali call per epoch; add a self-test asserting the hook fires exactly once per epoch, on a loader whose dataset.set_type == 1 (val), and that it never fires for the test loader.

issues.issue: The sensitivity self-test 'recorded val MSE equals an independent recompute on that checkpoint' cannot pass as worded for TFPS: val MSE at that epoch was computed with the noisy eval router (SparseMoE.py:59) and a shuffled, drop_last val loader (data_factory.py:28-30), both drawn from the global RNG at that point in training. A recompute will differ unless that RNG state is restored.
issues.evidence: layers/SparseMoE.py:57-60 (no self.training guard); data_provider/data_factory.py:28-30.
issues.fix: Save torch/np/python RNG state immediately before each val pass; the self-test restores it and reproduces the val MSE to 1e-6; alternatively state the tolerance as a noise-band and test only bit-exact for the deterministic baselines.

issues.issue: Baseline lr-selection value is not returned by the code. EarlyStopping stores it in val_loss_min (tools.py:47,69) but the object is a local of train() (official exp_main.py:112) and train() returns only the model (:215-217). The printed value (tools.py:67) has 6 decimals, which can create spurious ties between lr runs. PREREG says 'the value EarlyStopping saved' without saying how it is obtained.
issues.evidence: utils/tools.py:40-69 (both repos, sha 80c2f839); patchtst_official exp/exp_main.py:4,112,204,215.
issues.fix: Pre-register the mechanism: replace exp.exp_main.EarlyStopping (imported by name at official exp_main.py:4) with a subclass that writes val_loss_min (full float) and best epoch to metrics.json at every save; self-test that it equals min over the per-epoch printed val losses and that the saved checkpoint's epoch matches. Lr selection reads only this file, never any test field.

issues.issue: Both run_longExp.py files default to itr = 2 (tfps run_longExp.py:91, official run_longExp.py:77) and loop over ii (tfps :132, official :118), training a second run with suffix _1 from the continued RNG stream. PREREG pins epochs/patience/lradj but not itr; an unpinned itr doubles every run's budget and creates a second candidate score per seed/lr that could be picked post hoc.
issues.evidence: tfps run_longExp.py:91,132-160; patchtst_official run_longExp.py:77,118-143; scripts/etth1.sh passes itr 1 for TFPS only.
issues.fix: Add '--itr 1' to the shared settings for every arm, and assert in the wrapper that exactly one setting directory/checkpoint exists per run.

issues.issue: D_gauss draw location is ambiguous: 'drawn from torch's global RNG right after torch.manual_seed(seed) inside EDESC construction'. Re-seeding inside EDESC would give both EDESC instances identical D and reset the stream for later modules; drawing from the global stream without re-seeding shifts every subsequent init and the whole training RNG stream relative to tfps_zero. Neither leaks test data, but the second makes arms 1 vs 2 differ in all other inits and data order too.
issues.evidence: layers/Cluster.py:30 (uninitialised Parameter); run_longExp.py:112-115 (global seeding before Exp construction).
issues.fix: Draw D from a dedicated torch.Generator seeded e.g. 30000+seed (+1 for the frequency instance), so the global stream, all other inits and the shuffle order are identical between tfps_gauss and tfps_zero at the same seed; optionally report a paired Δ as a descriptive check alongside the Welch rule.

issues.issue: EarlyStopping with a NaN val loss: score = NaN, the comparison at tools.py:55 is False, so it saves and resets the counter every epoch; the run goes the full 100 epochs and the 'best' checkpoint is the last epoch. The failure rule covers non-finite training loss and primary score but not a non-finite val loss with finite train loss (possible via F.kl_div(pred.log()) at eval).
issues.evidence: utils/tools.py:50-63; layers/Cluster.py:77.
issues.fix: Add 'any non-finite val loss' to the failed-run definition.

issues.issue: Variance-triggered extension: the rule is mechanical (half-width only), so it cannot be steered towards a direction, but it is a data-dependent second look taken after test scores are visible, and 'every arm' includes the 4-lr baseline search.
issues.evidence: PREREG §7 Reachability.
issues.fix: Before running the extension, commit (git) the n=5 per-run score files and the computed half-widths; report the n=5 table alongside the n=10 verdict; state that the extension reruns the full lr grid for baselines (4x per seed) and that lr is re-selected per new seed by the same rule.

issues.issue: Budget asymmetry by design: baselines get best-of-4 lr on val per seed (4 training runs), TFPS gets 1 run at an authors' lr whose selection procedure (val vs test) cannot be verified from the code; if the authors chose it on test, TFPS inherits that selection. Owner decision 6 accepts this.
issues.evidence: PREREG §5; scripts/etth1.sh:77-89,133-145.
issues.fix: State explicitly in §9 that the TFPS lr is an external choice of unknown provenance (possibly test-informed) and that Q3 cannot separate method gain from that choice.

issues.issue: Checkpoint path handling: train() uses args.checkpoints (exp_main.py:145) but test(test=1) hard-codes './checkpoints/'+setting (tfps exp_main.py:282, official :224). Sensitivity checkpoint must not overwrite checkpoint.pth (tools.py:68 writes that fixed name).
issues.evidence: tfps exp/exp_main.py:145,272,282; utils/tools.py:68.
issues.fix: Eval-only pass loads the checkpoint by absolute path recorded in provenance (with sha256), never via test(test=1); sensitivity checkpoint saved as checkpoint_valmse.pth in the same run directory.

lenses.summary: The Q2 and Q3 rules are exhaustive (each ends in INCONCLUSIVE), first-match-wins gives a consistent order, and every label can be reached in both directions when seed sd is <= ~0.005. Three things need fixing before FREEZE: (1) the reachability paragraph is wrong for SHRINKS and for unequal variances; (2) the extension trigger is not an exact formula; (3) the 'for some B' negative rules are a union over two baselines, so if the paper's claim is exactly true they fire about 8% of the time rather than 5%. Nothing here is blocking.

issues.issue: The reachability/power paragraph (§7) says SURVIVES, SHRINKS and VANISHES all need half-width < m_H. That is wrong both ways. SHRINKS (L>0 and U<m) needs 2*hw < m, i.e. hw < m/2, and so does the 'INIT MATTERS, smaller than m_H' sub-label. SURVIVES and VANISHES have no half-width requirement: with a wide CI they can still fire from the point estimate (VANISHES then needs d_hat < 0). Only INIT EQUIVALENT strictly needs hw < m. The paragraph also assumes df ~ 8 (equal sd). If DLinear's seed sd is much smaller than TFPS's (likely, since DLinear is deterministic and TFPS has eval noise), Welch df falls to ~4-6 and t to 1.95-2.12.
issues.evidence: Arithmetic: n=5, equal sd: df 8.00, t 1.860, hw 1.176*sigma (the prereg is correct here). sd ratio 0.1: df 4.08, t 2.120, hw 0.953*sigma_T. n=10 equal: df 18, t 1.734, hw 0.775*sigma. n=5 vs n=4 (one failed run): df 6.6, hw 1.284*sigma. Reaching SHRINKS needs sigma < 0.0047 (H=192) / 0.0030 (H=336) at n=5 and < 0.0071 / 0.0045 at n=10. Monte Carlo with a true gain of m/2: P(SHRINKS) = 0.97 at sd 0.002, 0.10 at sd 0.005, 0.002 at sd 0.01 (H=192).
issues.fix: Rewrite the paragraph per label: EQUIVALENT needs hw<m_H; SHRINKS and the 'smaller than m_H' sub-label need hw<m_H/2; SURVIVES/VANISHES/REVERSED have no hw floor. Quote Welch-Satterthwaite df for an sd ratio of 1 and of 0.1, and the sigma thresholds at n=5 and n=10. State that SHRINKS is effectively reachable only if seed sd <= ~0.003-0.005.

issues.issue: The extension trigger is not specified exactly. 'Any Q2/Q3 rule is unreachable because the half-width exceeds m_H' does not match its own criterion, because SHRINKS is already unreachable once hw > m_H/2. It also leaves open which CIs count (Δ, d_patchtst, d_dlinear, the paired Q2b?), which n to use after a failure, and who computes it.
issues.evidence: Simulation with trigger = max hw over {Δ, d_patchtst, d_dlinear} > m_H at n=5. P(extend) at H=192: 0.00 for sd 0.005, 0.57-0.83 for sd 0.01, ~1.0 for sd 0.02. At H=336: 0.22-0.41 for sd 0.005, 0.95-1.0 for sd 0.01. Type-I error of a single 5% one-sided bound under the null: fixed n=5 gives 0.046-0.047 (Welch is conservative); with the extension it is 0.050-0.057, highest when P(extend) is about 0.5. The inflation is small and stays near nominal.
issues.fix: Write it as a formula: extend at horizon H iff max(hw_Δ, hw_patchtst, hw_dlinear) > m_H, computed from the n=5 per-seed scores (n=4 for an arm with one failed run). Q2b is excluded. A script computes and commits the trigger from per-seed scores before any verdict table or label is printed. Say plainly that SHRINKS can stay unreachable after extension, and record the extension's ~0.5-1 pp type-I inflation (or accept it explicitly).

issues.issue: Burden of proof leans against the paper in Q3's negative rules. REVERSED ('U_B<0 for some B'), VANISHES ('for some B, L<=0 and U<m') and the SHRINKS/SURVIVES split ('U_B<m for at least one B') are unions over two baselines at 5% each. Intersection-union protects the positive 'TFPS better' conclusions but not these. If the paper's claim is exactly true (d_B = m_H for both B), the chance that the claimed margin is wrongly excluded is about 8%, not 5%.
issues.evidence: Monte Carlo with true d=m for both baselines and the TFPS arm shared: P(U_1<m) = 0.047 for one baseline vs P(any U_B<m) = 0.082 (sd 0.005 or 0.01, n=5). With true d=0: P(REVERSED) = 0.07-0.09 vs 0.05 nominal.
issues.fix: Use Bonferroni over the two baselines for the union conditions: U_B (in REVERSED, VANISHES and the SHRINKS/SURVIVES split) comes from a one-sided 97.5% bound, and L_B > 0 keeps 95% (intersection-union needs no correction). Alternatively, keep 90% CIs and state in §7 that the family-wise rate of the 'some B' labels is ~8-10%.

issues.issue: The failed-run rule drops failures, which can favour the arm that fails. If a failure is arm-specific (e.g. D_gauss N(0,1) blowing up the aux loss, or TFPS at lr 5e-3), dropping that seed and using n=4 removes the worst outcome. The rule is also only written for n=5 ('>=2 failed seeds'), not for n=10. For baselines it does not say what happens when one lr-grid run is non-finite.
issues.evidence: §6: 'Failed runs are reported, not replaced... with 1 failure, verdicts use n = 4.' There is no rule for n=10 and no rule for failures within the lr grid.
issues.fix: (a) Any label that rests on an arm with a failure gets the suffix '— k FAILED RUN(S) IN <arm>'. Report a sensitivity where the failed seed is scored as that arm's worst observed seed. (b) BLOCKED if >=2 of 5 fail, or >=3 of 10 after extension. (c) A baseline lr run with non-finite val loss cannot be selected; the baseline seed counts as failed only if all 4 lr runs are non-finite. (d) Q3 is BLOCKED if tfps_gauss or either baseline is BLOCKED at that horizon. Q2 is BLOCKED if arm 1 or arm 2 is.

issues.issue: The VANISHES label claims more than its rule shows. The rule shows 'no gain detected and gain < m_H', not 'gain ≈ 0'. With a true gain of m/2 the label fires 35-52% of the time. SURVIVES is the mirror case: it needs only L>0 and m not excluded, so with a true gain of m/2 it fires 16-32%.
issues.evidence: Monte Carlo, d=m/2: H=192 sd 0.005 VANISHES 0.52 / SURVIVES 0.20; sd 0.01 VANISHES 0.45 / SURVIVES 0.16. H=336 sd 0.005 VANISHES 0.47 / SURVIVES 0.18.
issues.fix: Define each label in words in §7 (VANISHES = 'gain not detected; claimed margin excluded'; SURVIVES = 'gain detected; claimed margin not excluded'). Print the point estimate and CI next to every label. Optionally rename VANISHES to 'NOT REPLICATED (< m_H)'.

issues.issue: The A < 0.30 qualifier is ambiguous: 'mean A over seeds' does not say which arm, and it requires both routers to fall below 0.30. Requiring both lets one router follow its affinity while the other does not, with no suffix (lenient to the paper). In arm 2, s is exactly uniform, so argmax s is a tie. torch then returns index 0 and A becomes P(top-1 = 0).
issues.evidence: Simulated A under the released noise (s + randn*softplus(s), 4 experts): uniform 0.250; s=(.28,.24,.24,.24) 0.267; (.3,.233,.233,.234) 0.277; (.4,.2,.2,.2) 0.332; (.55,.15,.15,.15) 0.415; (.7,.1,.1,.1) 0.491; one-hot 0.616. The threshold 0.30 = 1/n + 0.05 is right and can go either way, but A only clears it if the largest s exceeds the rest by about 0.1 or more.
issues.fix: The qualifier uses arm 1 (tfps_gauss) only, and arm 2 is a reported reference. Apply the suffix per router (TIME / FREQ) when that router's mean A < 0.30, naming which. Document how ties are handled in arm 2. Report A's distribution across seeds as well as its mean.

issues.issue: Q2 has a small asymmetry. INIT MATTERS gets a 'smaller than m_H' sub-label but INIT REVERSED gets none when its CI lies inside (0, m_H). There is also no item-level rule for Q2 or for horizons that are BLOCKED or PREMISE FAILED. The BLOCKED and premise checks should be stated as rule 0, ahead of the first-match list.
issues.evidence: §7 Q2 rules 1-4 and the parenthetical; the item-level rule is defined only for Q3.
issues.fix: Add 'INIT REVERSED, smaller than m_H'. Make BLOCKED / PREMISE FAILED rule 0. Apply the same-label-or-MIXED rule to Q2 and Q2b. A BLOCKED horizon appears as 'MIXED (192: …, 336: BLOCKED)'.

issues.issue: Using the paper's best-baseline margin m_H for both PatchTST and DLinear is a choice that should be stated. Against a baseline the paper beats by more than m_H, this makes SURVIVES easier and VANISHES/SHRINKS harder: lenient to the paper and conservative for the audit, which is acceptable. SHRINKS against that baseline would then not mean 'smaller than claimed against B'.
issues.evidence: §1 defines m_H from the best baseline (DLinear at 192; TSLANet/iTransformer at 336), while Q3 compares with PatchTST and DLinear.
issues.fix: Keep m_H as the one gate and state why. Also report each baseline's own paper margin (TFPS minus B in Table 1 [Q]) next to its CI, not gating.

issues.issue: The per-seed score is correct, with two things to state. Every window has pred_len×7 elements, so the mean of per-window MSEs equals utils/metrics.MSE over the concatenated array. Windows overlap (stride 1) and are strongly autocorrelated, so window-level tests are invalid. All inference is across training seeds and conditional on the fixed test set.
